title: Microsoft Purview Data Security Investigations: pre-built search templates for common scenarios
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, role controls, audit operations and consumption billing are supported. It appropriately separates the roadmap's template description from the surrounding DSI documentation and leaves template-specific settings and behaviour open.

claims.claim: Microsoft added pre-built search templates for common data security scenarios in DSI.
claims.quote: We're adding pre-built search templates to Microsoft Purview Data Security Investigations. Templates provide pre-configured search queries for common data security scenarios

DSI lets investigators search Microsoft 365 content relevant to a security incident.

claims.quote:
The Search tab includes three options:
- Query builder: Search for content based on keywords, file types, dates, and other conditions.
- Audit: Use audit search to identify content based on user activities recorded in the unified audit log.
- Endpoint DLP

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: DSI uses consumption billing based on stored data and AI compute rather than a dedicated enterprise plan or licence.
claims.quote: Billing in Data Security Investigations is based solely on the combination of the amount of stored data and the associated computing capacity needed for AI analysis. It isn't based on a dedicated enterprise plan or license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meters; rationale: cost
claims.claim: DSI storage is pay-as-you-go per GB per month for data associated with all investigations.
claims.quote: The storage meter for Data Security Investigations uses the pay-as-you-go billing model. You pay for storage on a gigabyte (GB) per month basis for stored data associated with all investigations in your organization.

claims.claim: Storage billing uses a linked Azure subscription.
claims.quote: Storage meter billing requires a link to an Azure subscription for pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing: Meters; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Storage charges start when items are added to an investigation's scope, including results of template-configured DSI searches.
claims.quote: Data storage charges start when you add items to the scope of an investigation.

claims.claim: Deleting an investigation stops paying for its associated stored data.
claims.quote: When you delete an investigation, you stop paying for the associated data storage amount. The charges are prorated to the number of days the data was stored in the billing cycle.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meters; rationale: cost
claims.claim: AI capacity uses pay-as-you-go DSI Compute Units and bills the units used.
claims.quote: Data Security Investigations uses the pay-as-you-go billing model for AI capacity. You need compute units for deep analysis and AI-related processing in your investigations. You pay only for the compute units you use.
